transcription.text: Hi, welcome to the EEVblog, an electronics engineering video blog of interest to anyone
involved in electronics design. I'm your host, Dave Jones. I got a message on my phone the other
day from one of these engineering recruitment consultants, one of these headhunters. You've
heard me mention them before in my engineering job interview tip blogs, and how useless they are and
just how annoying they can be. And I got a message from them and nothing unusual there. I get them
all the time because my resume is on every database from here, Timbuk2. So every month or
two at least, I get a phone call from a headhunter telling me, am I interested in some job here or
there or anything? But this one was a little bit different. Actually, it's not all that different
because about probably two or three times a year, I get this same phone call. And it's from these
recruitment companies, and it's not to tell me about a job that they've got that they think I
might be interested in, that my skills match up with their job they've got in line. No. What they
want is my advice on the job that they've got and what people can fill it, what people are best to
fill that role. And it ticks me off. You've got to be kidding me. These people phone me up, okay?
These are supposedly professional engineering recruitment consultants. Their job is to match
up your skills with a particular job for a client and then get you together and get a job. So you
would think that they know how to perform their job. Their job is to understand what the client's
needs are and find people to match them. But no. I get these idiots phoning me up, asking me for my
professional advice on, for free of course, asking me my advice on what people would be suitable
for a particular job or what some engineering jargon means or something like that. You've got
to be shitting me. No wonder they're working as bloody headhunters because they're useless. They
wouldn't survive in the engineering industry. You know, a good lot of them have engineering degrees
and they don't know jack. But that's not uncommon. But let's not go there. You know, when this sort
of thing started happening to me, when I started getting these phone calls for the advice for these
headhunters, they, you know, I gave my advice. You know, I didn't tell them off or anything like that
because, you know, I like to be helpful and I like to give advice. That's why I'm doing this blog.
And, but no, they just keep, these phone calls just keep on coming. I'm getting sick of it. So next
time one of them calls me up, I'm not going to, I'm not going to tell them off. No, I won't go mad.
I'll just say, I'll send you a link to a thing that'll be very helpful for you. It'll be this
video. And yes, you who just called me up, you're an idiot. So learn how to do your damn job and do
it properly. Otherwise get the hell out of the industry because guys like me, engineers, don't
want to put up with it. We think you're morons. So that's the end of that. I don't want to get started.
Yes, I haven't even started on recruitment consultants, but it leads me to one or two
other things which have ticked me off lately. The other thing that really ticks me off are local
component suppliers. And I get this all the time. Okay. One of the things they do is they phone you
up. They, you know, they cold call you up and they say, oh, we've got the representative from
Intel in town and they want to meet with you. What? What? What? Where does this come from?
They want to meet with me? Wow. They flew all the way from America to Australia just to meet me.
Wow. I must be so special. Oh, wow. Thanks. Yeah. Bring them over. We'll have some coffee. We'll
chat for hours and hours and we'll waste all my time just so that you can entertain your damn
suppliers and show them that you're actually doing your job, supposedly doing your job by trying to
get to clients in the country. Bugger off. No, go away. I don't want to meet them. If you invite
them over here saying you can meet all these people at various companies, you know, network
with them and all that sort of stuff. No, I'm not interested. Bugger off. The other thing these
suppliers do is they want to keep in contact with you. They keep phoning you up saying, oh, I'm
passing by. I want to drop in for a chat and see what projects you're working on. And if we can
help you, you know, oh, what can we, you know, we've got these new range of chips. If we think
that we can help you on the new project or what can we do? Can we offer any engineering advice
to you and things like that? No, go away. I'm a professional design engineer. I don't need
design advice from a component supplier. I'm perfectly capable of finding my own parts.
And if I need your help, I'll call you up. That's your only role. Your role is to just be there when
I call you, not for you to call me and offer advice. I don't need any. Go away, please.
You know what really ticks me off? You know what really gets under my skin? Are these manufacturers
who on their websites, they make you register to get data sheets. You've got to put all your
information in and then they'll email you the link to the damn data sheet. What is that? It's pure
engineering evil. That's what it is. I'm not going to use your damn parts because you're so annoying.
I'm going to go to someone else who just freely gives me the data sheets exactly what I want. I
don't want you to waste more of my time getting my contact details to make me jump through all
these hoops to get data sheets. Bugger off. Give me the information and I might consider using your
parts. And in case you're wondering, no, I haven't had a bad day. That's just normal.
